title: RICS Homebuyers Reports
blocks: The RICS Homebuyers Report, also known as a ‘home survey’ or ‘house survey’, is ideal for properties up to 100 years old. The survey can be carried out with or without a property valuation.

This is the most common and popular choice of report produced for a purchaser, giving essential information on specific property related defects, advice on repairs, maintenance and upgrading. This type of report is essential prior to your commitment to purchase.

Buying a house or flat in the UK is a major investment and understanding what you’re purchasing is essential. At Paul Fox Estate Agents, we help home buyers across Lincolnshire and South Yorkshire make confident property decisions with a professional RICS Home Survey.
Before you commit to buying, our trusted surveyors provide clear, expert insight into the true condition of your potential new home.
Do I need a house survey?

A house survey (also known as a home survey or property survey) provides an independent assessment of a property’s condition. It highlights structural issues, defects and maintenance concerns, so you know exactly what you’re buying.
Your home is one of the biggest financial commitments you’ll ever make. A professional home survey helps you avoid unexpected repair costs, negotiate a fair price, and move forward with confidence.

title: RICS Condition Report
blocks: The RICS Condition Report is a concise report detailing the condition of a property. Much like the Homebuyer Report, information is gained on property specific defects alongside repair and maintenance considerations.

title: RICS Building Survey
blocks: The RICS Building Survey is an extensive written report, similar in many ways to the RICS Homebuyer Report, but undertaken and delivered in much more detail. The report offers the client an in depth understanding of the building fabric, its fittings and the condition of all elements. This type of report is recommended on properties built pre 1900, listed buildings, or properties in a poor state of repair.

title: Insurance Valuations
blocks: These valuations are vital in ensuring you know how much to insure your property for. This report details the cost to rebuild the property. The calculation is carried out online using the BCIS Cost Calculator. An inspection of your home will be necessary in order to gather information relating to property specifics including age, type and size of the property. If you under insure your property, you may not be fully covered in the event you suffer a loss and in extreme cases where the property has to be re-built, the shortfall could leave you in financial difficulty. In the event of you being over insured this means you will be overpaying on your insurance.

title: Matrimonial Valuations
blocks: The use of an independent expert to provide a valuation of your shared home or assets (Residential and/or Commercial) is vital for both parties when a long term relationship is coming to an end. This enables you to gain an understanding of the up to date valuation of the property so that you can continue with proceedings. This report is used by the Solicitor’s involved and often by the court when and where required. We are often appointed jointly by both parties and are unbiased in our deliverance of the report, ensuring that we adhere to strict standards and guidelines. Matrimonial Valuations are carried out by Paul Fox MRICS FNEA or Liam Fox MRICS who are both RICS Registered Valuers and Chartered Surveyors.

title: Probate Valuations / Inheritance Tax Valuations
blocks: Paul Fox Surveyors and Valuers have a thorough understanding of the valuation required in order to comply with Her Majesty’s Revenue and Customs (HMRC). The valuation report is concise but sufficient in giving detail on many property specifics including size, location and condition and will also detail a list of non-essential and essential repairs. Due to the nature of the situation, our experienced team will be able to guide you through the process with ease, empathy and complete compassion ensuring that the valuation is provided with as little disruption as possible during this most difficult time.

title: Leasehold Extension Valuations/ (Leasehold Enfranchisement)
blocks: If you have a lease on a Residential property, you will only have it for a fixed period of time. The lease will tell you how many years you will own the property in effect. Ownership of the property returns to the Landlord when the lease comes to an end. Most flats are Leasehold. Houses can be Leasehold too.
You can ask the Landlord to extend your lease at any time. You may be able to extend your lease by:
90 years on a flat (If you qualify)
50 years on a house (If you qualify)

It is widely acknowledged that Mortgage Lenders look unfavourably at property with a lease unexpired of less than 75 years, and in some cases of less than 85 years unexpired. This can mean that at the point of a sale, the mortgage lender will put onus on the seller to get an extension of the lease prior to exchange of contracts and in some cases this has been known to take some time.

Due to the significant number of properties that are Leasehold, it is important that you appoint a competent Chartered Surveyor to provide you with an accurate calculation which can be provided by ourselves from a visit to the property.

So if you are concerned about the length of your lease and are considering the possibility of extending you lease, then please call us today or complete our online form so we can assist you in this matter.

title: Council Tax Valuations
blocks: Council Tax is something most of us will have to pay for all of our lives. The Valuation Office Agency is responsible for Council Tax Valuations and they ensure that bands are kept up to date in both England and Wales. Valuation bands in England are based on the level of Value of the property as at 1st April 1991 and not what the property is worth today.
Are you concerned that your Council Tax banding is incorrect? Do you need assistance in the preparation of a valuation of you home for Council Tax purposes?
Please call us today and find out how we can assist you.

title: Energy Performance Certificates (EPC’s)
blocks: Here at Paul Fox, we have been producing Energy Performance Certificates now for over 10 years on 1000s of Residential properties. We have a dedicated in house team of Domestic Energy Assessors able to provide EPC’s on a wide range of type and size dwellings.

It is a Government requirement for properties that are to be sold or let have a current EPC. You may also wish to get an EPC carried out on your home even if you are not selling or renting it, so that you are fully aware of its Energy Performance and the measures you are able to take in order it improve its Energy Efficiency and its rating.

It is important to consider that an EPC lasts for 10 years from the date of issue, subsequently, should you carry out any improvements within this time you should consider having a new EPC provided so that you are aware of its up to date rating.

From April 2018, The Energy Efficiency (Private Rented Property) (England and Wales) Regulations 2015 will bring into force minimum energy efficiency standards (MEES) in the Residential and Commercial private rented sector. From April 1st 2018 it will be unlawful to grant new leases of residential or commercial property with an EPC rating below an ‘E’.

title: Site Supervisions on New Homes
blocks: Paul Fox have been providing 10 year Structural Warranty Certificates on new dwellings for over 30 years in and around the North Lincolnshire region. Our clients have included many self-build projects for someone with the dream and desire to build their own home and also many local builders.

The Warranty includes a total of 10 stage inspections throughout the period of construction from start to practical completion. Interim Certificates (CML- Council of Mortgage Lenders) can also be provided to your mortgage lender where required. It should be recognised that such Certificates are vital and many Mortgage Lenders request these prior to sale completion.
Fees start from £1500. We also offer a 7 year Structural Warranty Certificate on Barn Conversions

title: Standard Purchase Report Valuations
blocks: Our standard valuation report covers property specifics in terms of age, size and type whilst delivering key information on a properties condition. The report is concise but detailed. These types of reports are produced often in cases where cash purchasers are not relying on a mortgage valuation and so we act to ensure that the price paid is fair and reasonable and reflects the current condition of the property.

title: Capital Gains Tax Valuations
blocks: Capital Gains Tax is a tax charged when you sell your property or asset and it has increased in value since the time of its acquisition. Due to Private Residence Relief, you usually will not be required to pay the tax on your own home. However, if you own more than one home or you use your home for business purposes, you may be required to pay Capital Gains Tax and a valuation will therefore be required.

Capital Gains Tax also applies where you intend to transfer the ownership of a share of a property or the entirety of it, then the value has to be assessed in order to pay the correct amount of Stamp Duty to the Local Authority. There are some exemptions to the tax in cases where you buy another property or assets for business use.
Here at Paul Fox, we have experienced Surveyors able to provide you with the necessary written valuation report required by the Inland Revenue.

title: Title Deed Plan Amendments
blocks: We prepare and provide Title Deed Plan amendments that are compliant with the HM Land Registry when you part sell or acquire a parcel of land to your existing property.
We are also capable of providing a new Title Deed Plan for new build properties or where an existing property is not registered with the HM Land Registry.

title: Immigrations Reports
blocks: For a number of years now, Paul Fox have carried out Immigration Reports. Such reports are required by the Home Office when a UK Resident wishes to bring over a family member from a Foreign Country. This can include:
Parents, grandparents and other dependent relatives.

The report requires an internal inspection of the property in order to establish its size, condition and current residents. This enables us to make a judgement on whether or not the property is capable of housing an additional person.
